_comment: Error-pattern matcher. Joe matches user input against `match` regex; if it hits, returns diagnosis + fixes. Languages: python, javascript, typescript, bash, git, generic.

patterns.title: NameError — variable doesn't exist
patterns.diagnosis: Python can't find a variable, function, or class named `{1}` in the current scope. Either it's misspelled, not imported, or referenced before it's assigned.
fixes: Check spelling — Python is case-sensitive (`Print` is not `print`).
If `{1}` comes from another module, did you `import` it?
If `{1}` is defined later in the file, move the definition above the line that uses it.
Inside a function: assign before referencing, use `global {1}`, or pass it as a parameter.

patterns.match: TypeError: unsupported operand type\(s\) for ([^:]+): '([^']+)' and '([^']+)'
patterns.title: TypeError — can't combine those types
patterns.diagnosis: Python doesn't know how to apply `{1}` between a `{2}` and a `{3}`. Most often this is mixing strings with numbers, or a `None` slipped in where a value was expected.
fixes: Convert one side: `int(x)`, `float(x)`, or `str(x)` so both sides match.
Check whether one operand is `None` — print it just before the line that fails.
If you're doing `'5' + 5`, decide which you want: `'5' + str(5)` or `int('5') + 5`.

patterns.title: TypeError — that thing isn't a function
patterns.diagnosis: You put `()` after `{1}` but it isn't callable. Usually this means a variable is shadowing a function name (e.g. `list = [1,2]` then later `list(...)`), or you used `()` instead of `[]` for indexing.
fixes: Did you assign over a builtin? Rename your variable (no more `list = ...`, `dict = ...`, `str = ...`).
If you meant to index, use `[]` not `()`.
Check what `{1}` actually holds by printing `type(it)` just before the call.

patterns.title: TypeError — can't index that
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote `thing[i]` but `thing` is a `{1}`, which doesn't support indexing. Common cause: trying to index into a function, generator, or `None`.
fixes: If `{1}` is `NoneType`, check whether a function silently returned `None`.
Generators aren't indexable — wrap with `list(gen)` first or use `next(gen)`.
If you have an `int` and meant a digit, convert: `str(n)[i]`.

patterns.title: TypeError — can't loop over that
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to iterate over a `{1}`, but it isn't iterable. Often this is iterating over an `int` or a function instead of a sequence.
fixes: If you meant a range of numbers, use `range(n)` not `n`.
If `{1}` is `NoneType`, check what produced it — a function that returned nothing?
Wrap single values in a list: `for x in [thing]:`.

patterns.match: TypeError: ([\w.]+)\(\) takes (\d+) positional arguments? but (\d+) (?:was|were) given
patterns.title: TypeError — wrong number of arguments
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` expects {2} positional arguments but got {3}. If this is a method, the extra one is probably `self` being passed implicitly.
fixes: Recount the arguments at the call site.
If `{1}` is a method, did you call it on an instance (`obj.method(x)`) or on the class (`Cls.method(x)`)? The class form needs `self` explicitly.
Did you forget to put `self` as the first parameter in the method definition?

patterns.match: TypeError: ([\w.]+)\(\) got an unexpected keyword argument '([^']+)'
patterns.title: TypeError — unknown keyword argument
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` doesn't accept a keyword argument called `{2}`. Either it's misspelled or the API changed.
fixes: Check spelling of `{2}`.
Look at the signature: `help({1})` or check the docs for the version you have installed.
If you upgraded a library, the parameter may have been renamed or removed.

patterns.title: TypeError — missing required argument
patterns.diagnosis: You called `{1}` without one of its required arguments.
fixes: Check the function signature with `help({1})`.
If this is a method, make sure you called it on an instance, not the class itself.
Provide the missing argument or give it a default value in the definition.

patterns.title: AttributeError — that attribute doesn't exist
patterns.diagnosis: A `{1}` doesn't have a `{2}`. The object is the wrong type, or the name is misspelled, or you're using an older/newer version of a library.
fixes: Print `type(obj)` and `dir(obj)` to see what attributes it actually has.
If `{1}` is `NoneType`, an earlier function returned `None` — chase that up.
Check spelling — `lenght` vs `length`, `append` vs `add`, etc.

patterns.title: AttributeError — module has no such attribute
patterns.diagnosis: The module `{1}` doesn't expose `{2}`. Common causes: name was removed in a newer version, you imported the wrong module, or a local file is shadowing the real one.
fixes: Check `dir({1})` to list what's actually available.
Do you have a local file named `{1}.py` shadowing the real package?
Check the version of the library and consult its changelog.

patterns.match: IndexError: list index out of range
patterns.title: IndexError — index past the end of the list
patterns.diagnosis: You asked for `lst[i]` where `i` is `>=` `len(lst)` (or `<` `-len(lst)`). The list is shorter than you expected, or your index calculation is off by one.
fixes: Print `len(lst)` and the index just before the line that fails.
Empty list? Check whether the data source returned anything.
Off-by-one — remember indexes go from `0` to `len(lst) - 1`.

patterns.match: IndexError: string index out of range
patterns.title: IndexError — string index past the end
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to read a character past the end of the string.
fixes: Check `len(s)` first.
Use slicing — `s[:n]` is safe even if `s` is shorter than `n`.
Empty input? Guard with `if s:`.

patterns.title: KeyError — missing dict key
patterns.diagnosis: The dict doesn't have a key matching `{1}`. Either it's spelled differently, the key has a different type (string vs int), or the dict was built without that key.
fixes: Use `d.get('{1}')` to return `None` instead of raising.
Use `if '{1}' in d:` to check first.
Print `list(d.keys())` to see what's actually there.

patterns.match: ValueError: invalid literal for int\(\) with base \d+: '([^']*)'
patterns.title: ValueError — can't parse that as an int
patterns.diagnosis: `int()` got `'{1}'` and can't turn it into a number. Common cause: whitespace, decimal point, or non-digit characters.
fixes: Use `int('{1}'.strip())` to remove whitespace.
If it might be a float string like `'3.14'`, use `int(float(x))`.
Validate with `s.isdigit()` before calling `int()`.

patterns.match: ValueError: too many values to unpack
patterns.title: ValueError — too many values to unpack
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote something like `a, b = iterable` but the iterable has more than two items.
fixes: Use `*rest` to absorb the extras: `a, b, *rest = iterable`.
Check the actual length: `print(len(list(iterable)))`.
Are you accidentally unpacking a string? `a, b = 'hi there'` would split into characters.

patterns.match: ValueError: not enough values to unpack \(expected (\d+), got (\d+)\)
patterns.title: ValueError — not enough values to unpack
patterns.diagnosis: You asked for {1} values but the iterable only has {2}.
fixes: Check the actual length before unpacking.
Provide defaults with a helper: `a, b = (lst + [None]*2)[:2]`.
If the source is a `str.split(...)`, pass `maxsplit` to guarantee count.

patterns.title: ZeroDivisionError — divided by zero
patterns.diagnosis: You divided by zero (or took `%` of zero). Somewhere a denominator slipped to `0`.
fixes: Guard with `if denom != 0:` before dividing.
Print the denominator just before the line that fails.
If averaging, return `0` (or `None`) when the count is zero.

patterns.match: FileNotFoundError: \[Errno 2\] No such file or directory: '([^']+)'
patterns.title: FileNotFoundError — file doesn't exist
patterns.diagnosis: Python can't find `{1}`. Either the path is wrong, you're in a different working directory, or the file truly isn't there yet.
fixes: Print `os.getcwd()` to see where Python is looking.
Use an absolute path or `pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / '{1}'`.
Check spelling and capitalization — `Data.txt` is not `data.txt` on case-sensitive filesystems.

patterns.title: PermissionError — not allowed to access that file
patterns.diagnosis: The OS refused the read/write. Either the file's permissions block you, or a directory above it is locked, or the file is open elsewhere (Windows).
fixes: Check permissions: `ls -l <path>` and `chmod` if you own it.
If on Windows, close the file in any other program first.
Don't write into system folders — use your home directory or a tmp dir.

patterns.title: IsADirectoryError — you gave a folder where a file is needed
patterns.diagnosis: You called something like `open(...)` on a path that points to a directory, not a file.
fixes: Append a filename: `open(folder / 'data.txt')`.
If you wanted to list the directory, use `os.listdir()` or `pathlib.Path(...).iterdir()`.

patterns.title: NotADirectoryError — that path isn't a folder
patterns.diagnosis: You treated a file as if it were a directory (e.g. `os.listdir(file_path)`).
fixes: Use `os.path.dirname(path)` to get the parent directory.
Check with `os.path.isdir(path)` before treating it as a folder.

patterns.title: ModuleNotFoundError — package isn't installed
patterns.diagnosis: Python can't find a package called `{1}`. Either it's not installed, you're using the wrong interpreter, or your virtualenv isn't activated.
fixes: Install it: `pip install {1}` (or `pip3 install {1}`).
If you have a venv, activate it first: `source venv/bin/activate`.
Check which python you're running: `which python` and `which pip` should point to the same place.
If `{1}` is a local module, make sure you're running from the right directory and there's an `__init__.py` if needed.

patterns.title: ImportError — that name isn't exported
patterns.diagnosis: Module `{2}` doesn't expose `{1}`. The name was renamed, removed, or you're hitting a circular import.
fixes: Check the docs for the version of `{2}` you have installed.
Look for circular imports — module A imports B which imports A.
Print `dir({2})` (after `import {2}`) to see what's actually there.

patterns.title: ImportError — relative import outside package
patterns.diagnosis: You used `from . import ...` but Python isn't treating the current file as part of a package.
fixes: Run from the project root with `python -m package.module`, not `python module.py`.
Add an `__init__.py` to the package directory.
Or switch to absolute imports: `from package.module import thing`.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — Python can't parse the line
patterns.diagnosis: Python tripped on the line marked by the caret. Most often: a missing colon, an unmatched bracket, or an `=` instead of `==`.
fixes: Check the previous line too — an unclosed `(` will report the error on the next line.
Did you forget `:` at the end of `if`, `for`, `def`, `class`?
Look for stray quotes or unmatched brackets.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — file ended too soon
patterns.diagnosis: Python reached the end of the file with something still open — usually an unclosed `(`, `[`, or `{`.
fixes: Match every opening bracket with a closer.
Most editors highlight matching brackets — jump back from the end of the file.
Check for an unfinished string literal.

patterns.match: SyntaxError: EOL while scanning string literal
patterns.title: SyntaxError — string never closed
patterns.diagnosis: A string opened with `'` or `"` never closed on the same line.
fixes: Add the matching closing quote.
If the string spans lines, use triple quotes: `"""..."""`.
Watch for an apostrophe inside a single-quoted string — `'don't'` breaks; use `"don't"` or escape it.

patterns.title: IndentationError — empty block
patterns.diagnosis: After a line ending in `:` (an `if`, `for`, `def`, `class`, etc.), Python expects an indented body.
fixes: Add at least one indented line below — `pass` if you want a placeholder.
Check the indent uses the same whitespace as the rest of the file (all tabs or all spaces).

patterns.title: IndentationError — indent levels don't line up
patterns.diagnosis: A line's indentation doesn't match any earlier indent level.
fixes: Make sure each block uses a consistent number of spaces (4 is standard).
Don't mix tabs and spaces — pick one and stick with it.
Most editors have a 'show whitespace' option to spot the mismatch.

patterns.match: TabError: inconsistent use of tabs and spaces
patterns.title: TabError — tabs and spaces mixed
patterns.diagnosis: Python sees tabs in some places and spaces in others within the same block.
fixes: Pick one (spaces — 4 is standard) and convert the file.
In VSCode: `Convert Indentation to Spaces` from the command palette.
Configure your editor to insert spaces when you press Tab.

patterns.match: UnboundLocalError: local variable '([^']+)' referenced before assignment
patterns.title: UnboundLocalError — used a local before assigning it
patterns.diagnosis: Inside a function, you read `{1}` before writing to it. Because the function assigns `{1}` somewhere, Python treats it as local, hiding any outer variable of the same name.
fixes: If you want the outer variable, add `global {1}` (or `nonlocal {1}` for an enclosing function) at the top of the function.
Or rename — don't shadow an outer name accidentally.
Initialize `{1}` at the top of the function before any conditional assignment.

patterns.title: RecursionError — too many recursive calls
patterns.diagnosis: A function called itself (directly or indirectly) too many times. Either the base case never fires, or the depth is genuinely huge.
fixes: Add a base case that returns without recursing.
Print the arguments at each call to see whether they converge toward the base case.
For very deep but legitimate recursion, rewrite as a loop, or `sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)` (with caution).

patterns.match: RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
patterns.title: RuntimeError — modified dict while iterating
patterns.diagnosis: You added or removed keys inside a `for k in d:` loop. Python forbids that because it'd skip or revisit items.
fixes: Iterate over a copy: `for k in list(d):` or `for k in d.copy():`.
Collect keys to remove first, then delete after the loop.
Use a dict comprehension to build a new dict instead of mutating in place.

patterns.title: StopIteration — iterator exhausted
patterns.diagnosis: An iterator has no more values, but something kept calling `next()` on it.
fixes: Use `next(it, default)` to return a fallback instead of raising.
Wrap with `try`/`except StopIteration:`.
Inside a generator, returning ends iteration cleanly — don't `raise StopIteration` manually (PEP 479).

patterns.match: OSError: \[Errno 28\] No space left on device
patterns.title: OSError — disk full
patterns.diagnosis: The disk (or the partition you're writing to) has no free space.
fixes: Check disk usage: `df -h`.
Clean up `~/.cache`, old logs, or build artifacts.
If writing to `/tmp`, switch to a partition with more room.

patterns.title: OSError — too many open files
patterns.diagnosis: The process hit its file-descriptor limit. Often this is from forgetting to close files or sockets in a loop.
fixes: Use `with open(...) as f:` so files close automatically.
Close sockets after use, especially in long-running scripts.
Raise the limit: `ulimit -n 4096` (shell) before running.

patterns.title: ConnectionRefusedError — server isn't listening
patterns.diagnosis: Nothing is accepting connections on the host/port you tried. The server is down, blocked, or on a different port.
fixes: Check the server is actually running.
Verify host and port — `telnet host port` or `nc -zv host port`.
Check firewall rules.

patterns.title: ConnectionResetError — peer dropped the connection
patterns.diagnosis: The other end of the connection closed it abruptly (RST). Often a server crash, idle timeout, or proxy reset.
fixes: Retry with backoff — transient resets are common.
Check server logs for crashes around the same time.
If long-lived connection, send keepalives.

patterns.title: TimeoutError — operation took too long
patterns.diagnosis: An I/O call exceeded its timeout.
fixes: Increase the timeout if the operation legitimately needs more time.
Add retries with backoff for flaky networks.
Check whether the remote service is overloaded.

patterns.title: socket.gaierror — DNS lookup failed
patterns.diagnosis: Python couldn't resolve the hostname to an IP. Either the name is wrong, DNS is broken, or there's no network.
fixes: Check spelling of the hostname.
Test resolution with `nslookup host` or `dig host`.
Verify network connectivity: `ping 8.8.8.8`.

patterns.title: UnicodeDecodeError — wrong encoding
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to decode bytes with `{1}` but they aren't valid `{1}`. The file is in a different encoding.
fixes: Try `encoding='utf-8'` if you used the default.
If it's a Windows file, try `encoding='cp1252'` or `'latin-1'`.
Use `errors='replace'` to substitute unknown bytes instead of raising.

patterns.title: UnicodeEncodeError — character not in target encoding
patterns.diagnosis: You're writing a character that `{1}` can't represent. Common when stdout/locale is ASCII and you print emoji or non-ASCII.
fixes: Specify `encoding='utf-8'` when opening the output file.
Set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` in your environment for stdout.
Use `errors='replace'` or `'ignore'` to skip bad characters.

patterns.title: JSONDecodeError — string isn't valid JSON
patterns.diagnosis: `json.loads` couldn't parse the input. Often: empty string, HTML error page, trailing commas, or single quotes.
fixes: Print the raw input — is it actually JSON or an HTML error page?
Strip whitespace before parsing.
JSON requires double quotes (not single) and no trailing commas.

patterns.title: pip not found
patterns.diagnosis: Your shell can't find `pip` on `PATH`. Maybe Python is installed but `pip` isn't on `PATH`, or you need `pip3`.
fixes: Try `pip3` instead of `pip`.
Use `python -m pip install ...` — works as long as Python itself is on `PATH`.
On macOS with Homebrew Python, `pip` may live next to `python3` in `/opt/homebrew/bin`.

patterns.title: pip — dependency resolution failed
patterns.diagnosis: pip can't find a combination of versions that satisfies every requirement.
fixes: Loosen version pins where you can.
Use `pip install --upgrade pip` — newer resolvers handle more.
Try resolving in a fresh virtualenv so existing packages don't constrain you.

patterns.title: pip — no matching distribution
patterns.diagnosis: pip couldn't find a build of `{1}` for your Python version and platform.
fixes: Check that the package name is correct and exists on PyPI.
Your Python version may be too old or too new for `{1}` — check its supported versions.
On Apple Silicon (M1/M2), some old wheels don't exist — try `--prefer-binary` or build from source.

patterns.title: pip — SSL certificate error
patterns.diagnosis: pip can't validate the TLS certificate of PyPI (or your mirror). Usually a system cert store issue or corporate proxy.
fixes: Update certs: `pip install --upgrade certifi`.
On macOS, run `/Applications/Python\ X.Y/Install\ Certificates.command`.
If behind a proxy, set `HTTPS_PROXY` and trust your corporate root cert.

patterns.title: pytest — collection error
patterns.diagnosis: pytest crashed importing a test file before it could run any tests. Usually a syntax or import error in the test module.
fixes: Run the test file directly: `python path/to/test_file.py` to see the underlying error.
Check imports at the top of the test file.
Use `pytest --collect-only` to narrow down which file fails.

patterns.match: RuntimeError: This event loop is already running
patterns.title: asyncio — event loop already running
patterns.diagnosis: You called `asyncio.run(...)` (or `loop.run_until_complete`) from inside an already-running loop. Jupyter, IPython, and some web frameworks already run a loop.
fixes: In Jupyter, just `await` the coroutine directly — no `asyncio.run`.
Use `nest_asyncio.apply()` if you really need nested loops.
Restructure so the outer code is also a coroutine.

patterns.match: Task was destroyed but it is pending|coroutine.*was never awaited
patterns.title: asyncio — coroutine never awaited
patterns.diagnosis: You created a coroutine but never `await`ed or scheduled it. Python warns because the work never ran.
fixes: Add `await` before the coroutine call.
Or schedule it: `asyncio.create_task(coro())`.
Make sure async functions called from sync code go through `asyncio.run(...)`.

patterns.title: AssertionError — assertion failed
patterns.diagnosis: An `assert` statement evaluated false. {1}
fixes: Read the message after `AssertionError:` for the specific check that failed.
If running with `python -O`, asserts are stripped — don't rely on them for production checks.
Replace with a real `if x: raise ValueError(...)` if it's a real validation.

patterns.title: NotImplementedError — method not implemented
patterns.diagnosis: Someone called a method that's defined as `raise NotImplementedError`, usually a placeholder in a base class.
fixes: Subclass and override the method.
Look at the docs for which methods you must implement.
If you wrote the stub yourself, fill it in!

patterns.title: Pickle error
patterns.diagnosis: Pickle couldn't serialize or deserialize the object. Common causes: nested function, lambda, open file, lock, or a class that's moved.
fixes: Top-level (module-level) functions pickle; lambdas and nested functions don't.
For unpickling, the class must be importable at the same path it was pickled from.
Consider `json` or `dill` if pickle keeps failing.

patterns.match: RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded while calling a Python object
patterns.title: RecursionError — runaway calls
patterns.diagnosis: Likely an infinite loop in `__getattr__`, `__repr__`, or similar dunder methods.
fixes: Inside `__getattr__`, use `object.__getattribute__(self, ...)` to avoid re-entering.
Inside `__repr__`, don't reference attributes that themselves trigger `__getattr__`.
Add a guard to break the loop.

patterns.title: pandas — SettingWithCopyWarning
patterns.diagnosis: You're assigning to a slice of a DataFrame, and pandas isn't sure whether you're modifying the original or a copy.
fixes: Use `.loc[row_idx, 'col']` for assignments instead of chained indexing.
If you want a copy, be explicit: `df2 = df[mask].copy()`.
The warning isn't always a bug, but treat it as one until you understand it.

patterns.title: pandas — can't convert column
patterns.diagnosis: A column has values that won't convert cleanly to the target dtype.
fixes: Use `pd.to_numeric(col, errors='coerce')` to turn bad values into `NaN`.
For dates, `pd.to_datetime(col, errors='coerce')`.
Inspect with `col[col.apply(lambda x: not pd.api.types.is_number(x))]`.

patterns.match: ValueError: (?:operands could not be broadcast together with shapes|could not broadcast input array from shape)
patterns.title: numpy — shape mismatch
patterns.diagnosis: Two arrays have shapes that can't broadcast together. Check the dimensions on each side.
fixes: Print `a.shape` and `b.shape` right before the operation.
Use `np.reshape`, `np.expand_dims`, or `np.broadcast_to` to align shapes.
Common cause: forgot to transpose a column vector.

patterns.title: numpy — dtype mismatch
patterns.diagnosis: An operation needs a different dtype than the array has.
fixes: Convert: `arr.astype(np.float64)` or `np.float32`.
Check `arr.dtype` before the operation.
Some functions require float input even when the array is int.

patterns.title: requests — connection failed
patterns.diagnosis: The HTTP request couldn't establish a connection. DNS, refused, no route, or TLS.
fixes: Check the URL — typo in the host?
Verify network connectivity to the host.
If it's a local server, is it running on the expected port?

patterns.title: requests — timeout
patterns.diagnosis: The HTTP request didn't complete within the timeout.
fixes: Increase: `requests.get(url, timeout=30)`.
Always pass a `timeout` — the default is none, which can hang forever.
Add retries via `urllib3.util.Retry` or `tenacity`.

patterns.title: requests — SSL error
patterns.diagnosis: TLS handshake failed. Cert expired, untrusted CA, hostname mismatch, or outdated `certifi`.
fixes: Update certifi: `pip install --upgrade certifi`.
Check the cert in a browser to see if it's valid.
As a last resort for self-signed dev servers: `verify=False` (don't ship this!).

patterns.title: requests — URL missing scheme
patterns.diagnosis: The URL is missing `http://` or `https://`.
fixes: Prepend `https://` to the URL.
Check whether you accidentally split a config value.

patterns.title: Django — database operational error
patterns.diagnosis: Django couldn't talk to the database properly. Connection refused, missing table, or locked.
fixes: Run `python manage.py migrate` if the schema is out of date.
Check `DATABASES` settings — host, port, credentials.
Make sure the database server is running.

patterns.title: Django — integrity constraint violation
patterns.diagnosis: A database constraint was broken — unique, foreign key, or `NOT NULL`.
fixes: Read the underlying SQL error for which constraint.
Check for `NULL` in a non-null column.
Use `get_or_create` if you might be inserting a duplicate.

patterns.title: Django — ImproperlyConfigured
patterns.diagnosis: Django's settings aren't set up correctly for what you're doing.
fixes: Make sure `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` is set in your environment.
Check `INSTALLED_APPS` includes any app you're using.
Some settings (`SECRET_KEY`, database `ENGINE`) are mandatory.

patterns.title: Flask — outside application context
patterns.diagnosis: You used something that needs the Flask app/request context (like `current_app`, `g`, `request`) outside a request handler.
fixes: Wrap in `with app.app_context():` for CLI / scripts.
For request-scoped things, only access them inside a route handler.
Background jobs need an explicit `app.app_context()` push.

patterns.title: Python/pip not on PATH
patterns.diagnosis: Your shell can't find `python` or `pip`. Either Python isn't installed, your venv isn't activated, or `PATH` doesn't include the install dir.
fixes: Activate your venv: `source venv/bin/activate`.
Try `python3` / `pip3` — `python` often points to Python 2 on older systems.
Check `PATH` includes the directory where Python lives.

patterns.title: `python` not found (Python 2 vs 3)
patterns.diagnosis: Many modern systems removed `python` (the unversioned name) and only ship `python3`.
fixes: Use `python3` explicitly.
On macOS install Python: `brew install python` and you'll get `python3`.
Make a symlink only if you understand what you're aliasing.

patterns.title: Looks like a typo for `print`
patterns.diagnosis: That looks like a misspelling of `print(...)`.
fixes: Use `print(...)` — p-r-i-n-t.
Most editors will auto-suggest builtins as you type.

patterns.title: Looks like a typo for `import`
patterns.diagnosis: That looks like a misspelling of `import`.
fixes: Use `import module` or `from module import thing`.

patterns.title: Looks like a typo for `input`
patterns.diagnosis: That looks like a misspelling of `input(...)`.
fixes: Use `input(prompt)` — i-n-p-u-t.

patterns.title: TypeError — list/str concatenation type mismatch
patterns.diagnosis: You used `+` between a sequence and a `{1}`. `+` only works between same-typed sequences.
fixes: Convert: `lst + list(other)` or `s + str(other)`.
Use `.append(x)` to add a single item to a list.
Use f-strings to build strings from non-strings: `f'{x}'`.

patterns.match: TypeError: can't multiply sequence by non-int of type
patterns.title: TypeError — non-int sequence multiplier
patterns.diagnosis: You did `sequence * x` where `x` isn't an `int`.
fixes: Use `int(x)` if `x` is a string of digits.
If you want element-wise math, use a numpy array or list comprehension.

patterns.match: TypeError: %d format: a number is required, not str
patterns.title: TypeError — old-style format wanted a number
patterns.diagnosis: `%d` needs an int but got a string.
fixes: Convert: `'%d' % int(s)`.
Or switch to f-string: `f'{s}'`.

patterns.title: TypeError — None can't be iterated
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to loop over `None`. A function probably returned `None` instead of a list/sequence.
fixes: Check what produced the value — `print(it)` just before the loop.
Functions that 'return nothing' implicitly return `None`. Make sure they `return []` or similar.
Guard with `for x in (it or []):`.

patterns.title: TypeError — None can't be indexed
patterns.diagnosis: You tried `obj[i]` but `obj` is `None`.
fixes: Whatever produced `obj` returned `None`. Trace it backward.
Check `if obj is not None:` before indexing.
Dict `.get(...)` returns `None` for missing keys — handle that.

patterns.title: AttributeError — None has no `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: You tried `.{1}` on `None`. Something earlier returned `None` instead of a real object.
fixes: Print the value just before the line that fails.
Did a function forget to `return`? Implicit returns are `None`.
Use `obj and obj.{1}` or `getattr(obj, '{1}', None)` to guard.

patterns.title: AttributeError — dict accessed like an object
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote `d.{1}` but `d` is a dict. Dicts use `d['{1}']`, not dot syntax.
fixes: Use `d['{1}']` to read.
Use `d.get('{1}')` to avoid a `KeyError`.
If you really want attribute access, use `types.SimpleNamespace(**d)` or a dataclass.

patterns.title: ImportError — circular import
patterns.diagnosis: Two modules import each other. One imports the other before it's finished loading.
fixes: Move the import inside the function where it's used (lazy import).
Refactor common code into a third module both can import.
Avoid `from a import x` style for the circular pair — `import a` then use `a.x` defers lookup.

patterns.match: TypeError: ([\w.]+)\(\) got some positional-only arguments passed as keyword arguments
patterns.title: TypeError — positional-only arg passed as keyword
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` declares some arguments as positional-only (after `/` in the signature). You passed one by name.
fixes: Drop the keyword: `f(value)` not `f(name=value)`.
Check the signature with `help({1})`.

patterns.match: TypeError: object\.__init__\(\) takes exactly one argument
patterns.title: TypeError — extra args passed to object.__init__
patterns.diagnosis: A parent class's `__init__` got arguments it doesn't accept, usually because `super().__init__(...)` was passed args meant for someone else.
fixes: Call `super().__init__()` with no args, unless the parent class explicitly accepts them.
Make sure your class hierarchy is sane — check `Cls.__mro__`.

patterns.title: KeyboardInterrupt — you hit Ctrl+C
patterns.diagnosis: Someone (probably you) pressed Ctrl+C. Python interrupted the program.
fixes: If this was unintended, just rerun.
To handle gracefully, wrap with `try / except KeyboardInterrupt:` and clean up.

patterns.title: SystemExit — program called sys.exit()
patterns.diagnosis: Something called `sys.exit()` (or `exit()`). That's how scripts end normally; only odd if you weren't expecting it.
fixes: Trace which code called `exit()` — often a CLI parser does this on bad args.
Inside tests, `pytest` catches `SystemExit` for you.

patterns.title: pandas/dict — missing key `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: You asked for a key/column called `{1}` that doesn't exist.
fixes: List actual columns: `df.columns.tolist()` or `list(d.keys())`.
Check for whitespace, capitalization, or hidden characters.
Use `df.get('{1}')` to return `None` instead of raising.

patterns.title: OverflowError — number too large
patterns.diagnosis: A float computation exceeded the largest representable value (Python ints can grow unbounded).
fixes: Use `decimal.Decimal` or `math.log` to keep things in range.
Check whether you really need an exponential or factorial that big.

patterns.title: FloatingPointError — invalid float op
patterns.diagnosis: Numpy/decimal raised on a floating-point exception (only if you set the policy).
fixes: Check inputs for `inf` / `NaN`.
`np.seterr(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore')` if you want to suppress.

patterns.title: UnicodeTranslateError
patterns.diagnosis: A `str.translate` failed on a character.
fixes: Make sure your translation table covers the characters in the input.
Try `errors='replace'` style handling upstream.

patterns.title: LookupError — invalid key or index
patterns.diagnosis: A generic lookup failed. Catches both `KeyError` and `IndexError`.
fixes: Catch the specific subtype where possible.
Validate keys/indices before lookup.

patterns.title: DeprecationWarning
patterns.diagnosis: You're using something that's planned for removal.
fixes: Read the warning text — it usually says what to use instead.
Pin the library version if you can't update yet.
Treat as `error` with `-W error::DeprecationWarning` to catch all instances.

patterns.title: NameError — `self` used outside a method
patterns.diagnosis: You used `self` outside a class method.
fixes: Inside a class, indent the function under `class:` and name the first parameter `self`.
If this is a standalone function, drop the `self.` prefix.

patterns.title: Pickle recursion limit
patterns.diagnosis: Pickling a deeply nested or self-referential object hit the recursion limit.
fixes: Use `dill` which handles more shapes than `pickle`.
Refactor data so it isn't self-referential.
Bump the limit cautiously: `sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)`.

patterns.title: argparse — missing required argument
patterns.diagnosis: You ran a CLI without one of its required arguments.
fixes: Pass `--help` to see the usage.
Add the missing argument on the command line.

patterns.title: argparse — unknown argument
patterns.diagnosis: You passed an argument the script doesn't define.
fixes: Check spelling against `--help`.
Quote arguments with spaces.

patterns.title: ResourceWarning — unclosed file/socket
patterns.diagnosis: Something was garbage-collected without being closed.
fixes: Use `with` blocks for files and sockets.
Run with `-W error::ResourceWarning` to catch leaks at the source.

patterns.title: TypeError — unhashable type
patterns.diagnosis: You used a `{1}` (a mutable type) as a dict key or set member. Only hashable (immutable) things can be hashed.
fixes: Convert lists to tuples: `tuple(my_list)`.
Convert sets to frozensets: `frozenset(my_set)`.
Use a different data structure if mutability is essential.

patterns.match: TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'
patterns.title: TypeError — bytes vs str
patterns.diagnosis: An API needs `bytes` but got a `str` (or vice versa).
fixes: Encode: `s.encode('utf-8')` to make bytes.
Decode: `b.decode('utf-8')` to make str.
Open files as `'rb'`/`'wb'` for bytes mode.

patterns.match: TypeError: '([^']+)' object does not support item assignment
patterns.title: TypeError — that thing is immutable
patterns.diagnosis: You tried `obj[i] = x` but a `{1}` is immutable.
fixes: Strings and tuples can't be modified in place — build a new one.
If `{1}` is `bytes`, use `bytearray` for mutability.

patterns.match: IndexError: tuple index out of range.*format|IndexError: Replacement index \d+ out of range
patterns.title: Format string — bad index
patterns.diagnosis: A `{...}` in your format string refers to a positional argument that wasn't provided.
fixes: Count `{}` placeholders vs args.
Switch to f-strings — they catch this at compile time.

patterns.title: Format string — missing key
patterns.diagnosis: A `{name}` placeholder references a keyword you didn't pass.
fixes: Pass it: `'Hi {name}'.format(name='Joe')`.
Use `.format_map(d)` with a `defaultdict(str)` to allow missing keys.

patterns.title: RuntimeWarning — invalid math
patterns.diagnosis: Numpy hit `NaN`/`inf`/divide-by-zero in elementwise math.
fixes: Filter out bad values before the op.
Use `np.where(...)` to short-circuit safely.

patterns.match: SyntaxError: positional argument follows keyword argument
patterns.title: SyntaxError — positional after keyword arg
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote something like `f(a=1, 2)` — once you start using keyword args, all later args must also be keywords.
fixes: Reorder: positional first, then keyword.
Or use names for all: `f(a=1, b=2)`.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — assignment in lambda
patterns.diagnosis: Lambdas can only contain expressions, not statements like `x = 1`.
fixes: Use `:=` (walrus) for assignment-expressions if Python 3.8+.
Define a `def` if you need statements.

patterns.match: SyntaxError: name '([^']+)' is parameter and global
patterns.title: SyntaxError — name is both parameter and global
patterns.diagnosis: You declared a function parameter as `global` inside the same function.
fixes: Remove the `global` declaration — the parameter is local.
Rename one of them.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — duplicate keyword argument
patterns.diagnosis: Same keyword used twice in a call.
fixes: Remove one of the duplicates.
If merging dicts, use `**{**a, **b}`.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — walrus on old Python
patterns.diagnosis: The `:=` walrus operator needs Python 3.8+.
fixes: Upgrade Python.
Rewrite without `:=`.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — `await` outside async function
patterns.diagnosis: You used `await` in a regular function. Only `async def` functions can `await`.
fixes: Change `def` to `async def`.
Or call the coroutine via `asyncio.run(coro())`.

patterns.title: TypeError — missing required init arg
patterns.diagnosis: A class's `__init__` was called without one of its required args.
fixes: Pass the missing arg when constructing.
Give it a default value in the `__init__` signature.
Check whether you're using a dataclass and need to set the field.

patterns.match: During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred
patterns.title: Exception during handling — chained
patterns.diagnosis: An `except` block itself raised. Python shows both.
fixes: Read the FIRST traceback — it's usually the real cause.
The second traceback is whatever your handler did wrong.

patterns.title: TypeError — abstract class
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to instantiate a class that has abstract methods.
fixes: Subclass it and implement all `@abstractmethod` methods.
Don't instantiate the base — make a concrete subclass.

patterns.title: RecursionError — runaway repr/str
patterns.diagnosis: `__repr__` or `__str__` calls itself.
fixes: Don't reference attributes that themselves trigger `__repr__`.
Use `object.__repr__(self)` as a base case.

patterns.title: Possible OrderedDict typo
patterns.diagnosis: An attribute call on `OrderedDict` failed.
fixes: Plain `dict` is ordered since 3.7 — you may not need `OrderedDict`.
Check the available methods with `dir(od)`.

patterns.title: TypeError — using subscript on non-generic
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote `Foo[int]` but `Foo` isn't a generic class.
fixes: Make `Foo` inherit from `Generic[T]`.
On older Python, use `from __future__ import annotations` for forward refs.

patterns.match: asyncio\.run\(\) cannot be called from a running event loop
patterns.title: asyncio.run inside running loop
patterns.diagnosis: You called `asyncio.run` while a loop was already running.
fixes: Use `await coro` instead.
Use `loop.create_task(coro())` in the existing loop.

patterns.title: BlockingIOError
patterns.diagnosis: A non-blocking I/O call would have blocked.
fixes: Use `select`/`selectors` to wait for readiness.
Or switch to blocking mode if appropriate.

patterns.match: maximum recursion depth exceeded while calling
patterns.title: Recursion depth exceeded
patterns.diagnosis: Recursion ran away. Check that the base case fires.
fixes: Print arguments at each call.
Convert to iteration if depth is genuinely needed.

patterns.match: TypeError: Cannot read propert(?:y|ies) (?:of undefined \(reading '([^']+)'\)|'([^']+)' of undefined)
patterns.title: TypeError — reading property of undefined
patterns.diagnosis: Something is `undefined` and you tried to read `.{1}{2}` on it. The variable wasn't assigned, an array index didn't exist, or an API returned nothing.
fixes: Add optional chaining: `obj?.{1}{2}`.
Default with nullish coalescing: `(obj ?? {}).{1}{2}`.
Trace where `obj` came from — print it just before the access.
Async result? Make sure you `await`ed it.

patterns.match: TypeError: Cannot read propert(?:y|ies) (?:of null \(reading '([^']+)'\)|'([^']+)' of null)
patterns.title: TypeError — reading property of null
patterns.diagnosis: Something is `null` and you tried to read `.{1}{2}` on it.
fixes: Use optional chaining: `obj?.{1}{2}`.
Check for null first: `if (obj) { ... }`.
`document.querySelector` returns `null` if not found — guard the result.

patterns.title: TypeError — `{1}` isn't a function
patterns.diagnosis: You called `{1}(...)` but `{1}` isn't a function. Either it's the wrong type, misspelled, or not imported.
fixes: Check `typeof {1}` just before the call.
If `{1}` is a method, did the import succeed? `console.log({1})` to inspect.
If a library API, check the version — the method may have been renamed.

patterns.title: TypeError — reassigning a const
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote `const x = ...` then later tried `x = ...`. `const` bindings can't be reassigned.
fixes: Use `let` if you need to reassign.
If you're mutating a property of a const object (`obj.x = 1`), that's allowed — only the binding is constant.

patterns.match: TypeError: Cannot set propert(?:y|ies) (?:'?([^'\s]+)'? of undefined|of undefined)
patterns.title: TypeError — setting property on undefined
patterns.diagnosis: You tried `obj.{1} = ...` but `obj` is `undefined`.
fixes: Ensure `obj` is defined first.
Guard with `if (obj) obj.{1} = ...`.

patterns.match: TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
patterns.title: TypeError — null/undefined where object needed
patterns.diagnosis: You passed `null`/`undefined` to something that needs an object — usually `Object.keys`, `Object.assign`, or spreading.
fixes: Default with `obj ?? {}`.
Check the value before the call.

patterns.title: ReferenceError — `{1}` doesn't exist
patterns.diagnosis: JS doesn't know what `{1}` is. Misspelled, not imported, scope issue, or browser-vs-node mismatch.
fixes: Check spelling.
If from another module, did you `import` it?
If `{1}` is a browser global (like `window`, `document`), is this code running in Node?
If `{1}` is a Node global (like `process`, `__dirname`), it won't exist in browser code.

patterns.title: ReferenceError — temporal dead zone
patterns.diagnosis: You read `{1}` before its `let`/`const` declaration line. `let`/`const` are hoisted but unreadable until the declaration runs.
fixes: Move the declaration above the use.
If `{1}` is inside a closure that runs early, restructure so the closure can see the final value.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — unexpected token
patterns.diagnosis: The parser hit something it didn't expect at that point.
fixes: Check the previous line for a missing `;`, `,`, `)`, or `}`.
If parsing JSON, the input may be HTML or an empty string.
Look for stray characters from a copy-paste.

patterns.match: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
patterns.title: SyntaxError — JSON ended too soon
patterns.diagnosis: `JSON.parse` got an empty string or truncated JSON.
fixes: Check the response body — was the request successful?
Log the raw text before parsing.
Empty body? Default to `{}` before parsing.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — unexpected identifier
patterns.diagnosis: An identifier sits where the parser expected a comma, operator, or `;`.
fixes: Check for a missing comma between object properties or array items.
If you pasted code, check for invisible characters.

patterns.match: SyntaxError: Identifier '([^']+)' has already been declared
patterns.title: SyntaxError — duplicate declaration
patterns.diagnosis: You declared `{1}` twice in the same scope with `let`/`const`/`class`.
fixes: Reassign with just `{1} = ...` (no `let`/`const`).
Rename one of them.
Check whether two files are merged together (bundling).

patterns.title: SyntaxError — missing closing paren
patterns.diagnosis: A function call has an unclosed `(`.
fixes: Match every `(` with `)`.
Look for a string with an unescaped quote that's eating the rest of the line.

patterns.title: SyntaxError — invalid token
patterns.diagnosis: Some character isn't legal here — could be a stray symbol or a typo.
fixes: Check the line for `&` instead of `&&`, `;` inside a string, or smart-quotes.
Copy-paste sometimes brings in `'` (curly quote) instead of `'`.

patterns.match: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
patterns.title: RangeError — infinite recursion
patterns.diagnosis: A function calls itself (directly or via mutual recursion) without ever reaching a base case.
fixes: Add a base case.
Check getters/setters that may trigger each other.
Convert to iteration if depth is needed.

patterns.title: RangeError — bad array length
patterns.diagnosis: You tried `new Array(n)` with a negative number or a non-integer.
fixes: Cast: `new Array(Math.max(0, Math.floor(n)))`.
Verify `n` is a sane integer.

patterns.title: Promise rejection not handled
patterns.diagnosis: A promise rejected and no `.catch` or `try/await` was around to handle it.
fixes: Add `.catch(err => ...)` to the promise chain.
Inside `async` functions, wrap the `await` in `try/catch`.
At top level, listen on `unhandledrejection` (browser) or `process.on('unhandledRejection', ...)` (Node).

patterns.title: Unhandled promise rejection
patterns.diagnosis: Node logs this when a promise rejects without a handler. Future Node versions will exit the process.
fixes: Always attach `.catch` or wrap `await` in `try/catch`.
Add `process.on('unhandledRejection', ...)` as a safety net.

patterns.title: Module not found — `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: Webpack/Vite/Node can't find `{1}`. Either not installed, wrong path, or a typo.
fixes: Install it: `npm install {1}`.
Check spelling and path — relative imports need `./` or `../`.
If using TypeScript, also check `tsconfig.json` paths.
Restart the dev server after installing.

patterns.match: ENOENT: no such file or directory(?:, (?:open|stat) '([^']+)')?
patterns.title: ENOENT — file/path not found
patterns.diagnosis: The OS can't find `{1}`. Wrong path, file not created yet, or you're in the wrong CWD.
fixes: Print `process.cwd()` to see where Node is looking.
Use an absolute path or `path.join(__dirname, '{1}')`.
Check spelling and case sensitivity.

patterns.title: EADDRINUSE — port already in use
patterns.diagnosis: Another process is already listening on that port.
fixes: Find it: `lsof -i :PORT` (macOS/Linux) or `netstat -ano | findstr :PORT` (Windows).
Kill the old process, or pick a different port.
If you killed your server but the port lingers, wait a few seconds for `TIME_WAIT`.

patterns.title: EACCES — permission denied
patterns.diagnosis: The OS won't let you read/write/listen there.
fixes: Don't run `npm` with `sudo` — use a node version manager like `nvm`.
Ports below 1024 need root on Linux/macOS — pick a higher port.
Check `ls -l` on the file/directory.

patterns.title: EMFILE — too many open files
patterns.diagnosis: Your process exceeded its file-descriptor limit.
fixes: Make sure file handles are closed (`fs.close`, end streams).
Raise the limit: `ulimit -n 4096`.
Use `graceful-fs` which queues opens.

patterns.title: MODULE_NOT_FOUND
patterns.diagnosis: Node can't find `{1}`. Either not installed, path is wrong, or you forgot `npm install`.
fixes: Run `npm install` to fetch dependencies.
For local imports, check the relative path and add the `.js` extension if using ES modules.
If `package.json` exists but `node_modules` doesn't, install.

patterns.title: require not defined (ESM context)
patterns.diagnosis: You used `require` in an ES module. ESM uses `import`.
fixes: Convert to `import x from 'y'`.
Or set `"type": "commonjs"` in `package.json` (or rename file to `.cjs`).
If you really need `require` in ESM, use `import { createRequire } from 'module'`.

patterns.title: import.meta outside module
patterns.diagnosis: `import.meta` only works in ES modules.
fixes: Set `"type": "module"` in `package.json`.
Rename file to `.mjs`.

patterns.match: SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
patterns.title: Cannot use `import` outside a module
patterns.diagnosis: Node treated this file as CommonJS but you used ES `import`.
fixes: Set `"type": "module"` in `package.json`.
Rename file to `.mjs`.
Use `require` if you intend CommonJS.

patterns.title: __dirname not defined (ESM)
patterns.diagnosis: ES modules don't have `__dirname`/`__filename` automatically.
fixes: Compute them: `const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`.
Switch back to CommonJS if you don't need ESM.

patterns.title: npm ENOENT
patterns.diagnosis: npm tried to read a file/directory that's missing. Often a typo in a script path or missing `package.json`.
fixes: Make sure you're in the right directory (one with `package.json`).
Run `npm install` to populate `node_modules`.

patterns.title: npm peer dependency conflict
patterns.diagnosis: A package wants a peer it can't find or that conflicts with another version.
fixes: Install the requested peer manually.
Use `--legacy-peer-deps` to bypass (only if you trust the result).
Look at the message — it names the conflicting versions.

patterns.title: npm ERESOLVE — dependency conflict
patterns.diagnosis: npm v7+ resolver found incompatible version ranges in your tree.
fixes: Read the message — it shows which packages conflict.
Update one of the conflicting packages.
`--legacy-peer-deps` falls back to the old behavior.

patterns.title: npm — package not found (404)
patterns.diagnosis: npm asked the registry for a package and got a 404.
fixes: Check the package name spelling.
If it's a private package, log in: `npm login`.
Check your `.npmrc` registry URL.

patterns.title: CORS error
patterns.diagnosis: The browser blocked a request because the server didn't send the right `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers.
fixes: Have the server send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <your-origin>`.
For dev only: use a proxy in your dev server to bypass.
Preflight `OPTIONS` requests need the server to respond correctly too.

patterns.title: Mixed content blocked
patterns.diagnosis: An HTTPS page tried to load an HTTP resource. Browsers block this.
fixes: Use HTTPS for all resources.
Update third-party URLs to their HTTPS form.
If you control the resource, redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

patterns.title: Connection refused
patterns.diagnosis: The browser couldn't connect — nothing listening at that host/port.
fixes: Is the server running?
Check the URL — right port, right host?

patterns.title: fetch failed
patterns.diagnosis: `fetch` couldn't complete — CORS, network down, mixed content, or DNS.
fixes: Check the URL is reachable in a browser tab.
Open devtools network tab for the underlying reason.
Verify CORS headers if cross-origin.

patterns.match: Uncaught ReferenceError: process is not defined
patterns.title: `process` not defined (browser)
patterns.diagnosis: `process` is a Node global. Browser code doesn't have it.
fixes: Use `import.meta.env` (Vite) or `process.env` polyfilled by your bundler.
Webpack/Vite can inject `process.env.X` at build time.

patterns.match: Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match
patterns.title: React — hydration mismatch
patterns.diagnosis: Server-rendered HTML doesn't match what React rendered on the client.
fixes: Avoid `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, or `window` checks in render.
Use `useEffect` to set client-only state after mount.
Make sure server and client see the same data.

patterns.title: React — invalid hook call
patterns.diagnosis: Hooks must be called at the top of a function component or another hook — not in a class, conditional, or non-component function.
fixes: Move the hook call to the top of the component body.
Don't put hooks inside `if`/`for`.
Check for two copies of React (run `npm ls react`).

patterns.match: Each child in a list should have a unique \"key\" prop
patterns.title: React — missing list key
patterns.diagnosis: When rendering arrays, each element needs a stable, unique `key` prop.
fixes: Use a stable id: `<Item key={item.id} />`.
Don't use the array index unless the list never reorders.
Make sure keys are unique across siblings.

patterns.match: Objects are not valid as a React child
patterns.title: React — rendered an object
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to render a plain object (or a Promise) directly. React renders strings, numbers, arrays of these, or elements.
fixes: Stringify: `{JSON.stringify(obj)}`.
Pick a specific field: `{obj.name}`.
If it's a Promise, `await` it before render or use Suspense.

patterns.match: Property '([^']+)' does not exist on type '([^']+)'
patterns.title: TS — property doesn't exist on type
patterns.diagnosis: TypeScript sees `{2}` and it doesn't declare `{1}`.
fixes: Add `{1}` to the type definition.
If you're confident at runtime, cast: `(obj as any).{1}`.
Use an index signature `[key: string]: T` if the type is dynamic.
Check imports — you may be importing a stale type.

patterns.match: Type '([^']+)' is not assignable to type '([^']+)'
patterns.title: TS — type not assignable
patterns.diagnosis: You're assigning a `{1}` where a `{2}` is expected.
fixes: Adjust the source value to match `{2}`.
Widen the target type if appropriate.
Use type assertion `as {2}` only when you know runtime is safe.

patterns.match: Cannot find module '([^']+)' or its corresponding type declarations
patterns.title: TS — module / types not found
patterns.diagnosis: TypeScript can't resolve `{1}`, or it has no type declarations.
fixes: Install types: `npm install --save-dev @types/{1}`.
If the package has no types, add `declare module '{1}';` to a `.d.ts` file.
Check `tsconfig.json` paths and `moduleResolution`.

patterns.title: TS — possibly null
patterns.diagnosis: TypeScript thinks the value could be `null` here.
fixes: Guard: `if (x !== null) { ... }`.
Optional chaining: `x?.prop`.
Non-null assertion (when you're sure): `x!.prop`.
Narrow earlier — early-return on null.

patterns.title: TS — possibly undefined
patterns.diagnosis: TS thinks the value could be `undefined` here.
fixes: Guard: `if (x) { ... }`.
Optional chaining: `x?.prop`.
Provide a default: `x ?? defaultValue`.

patterns.match: Argument of type '([^']+)' is not assignable to parameter of type '([^']+)'
patterns.title: TS — bad argument type
patterns.diagnosis: You're passing a `{1}` where a `{2}` is needed.
fixes: Convert the value to match.
Loosen the parameter type if appropriate.
Check if you're passing the right variable.

patterns.title: TS — no exported member `{2}`
patterns.diagnosis: The module `{1}` doesn't export `{2}`.
fixes: Check spelling.
Open the file and see what it actually exports.
If types lag the runtime, you may need `@ts-ignore` temporarily.

patterns.match: Conversion of type '([^']+)' to type '([^']+)' may be a mistake
patterns.title: TS — possibly mistaken cast
patterns.diagnosis: You used `as` between two unrelated types.
fixes: Cast through `unknown` first: `x as unknown as Target`.
Reconsider — usually a cast like this signals a bug.

patterns.title: Webpack — module parse failed
patterns.diagnosis: Webpack can't parse a file. Often missing loader for that file type.
fixes: Add an appropriate loader (`babel-loader`, `ts-loader`, etc.).
Check the file is the format webpack expects.
If importing CSS/SVG, configure the right rule.

patterns.title: Vite — HMR error
patterns.diagnosis: Hot Module Replacement failed to apply an update.
fixes: Save the file again after fixing any syntax error.
Hard reload the browser if HMR gets stuck.
Check the terminal for the actual error message.

patterns.title: Looks like `const` typo
patterns.diagnosis: That's probably meant to be `const`.
fixes: Use `const x = ...` for constants.

patterns.title: Looks like `length` typo
patterns.diagnosis: `.lenght` should be `.length`.
fixes: Use `.length` (l-e-n-g-t-h).

patterns.title: Looks like `receive` typo
patterns.diagnosis: `recieve` should be `receive` (i before e except after c).
fixes: Spell it `receive`.

patterns.match: Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected strict mode reserved word
patterns.title: Reserved word in strict mode
patterns.diagnosis: You used a name reserved in strict mode (like `arguments`, `eval`, `implements`).
fixes: Rename the variable.

patterns.match: TypeError: (?:Converting circular structure to JSON|cyclic object value)
patterns.title: Circular reference in JSON
patterns.diagnosis: `JSON.stringify` hit an object that references itself.
fixes: Pick only safe fields to serialize.
Use a replacer that tracks seen objects.
Libraries like `flatted` handle cycles.

patterns.match: TypeError: Promise resolver .* is not a function
patterns.title: Promise constructor needs a function
patterns.diagnosis: `new Promise(...)` needs an executor function, not a value.
fixes: Call: `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... })`.
Use `Promise.resolve(x)` to wrap a value.

patterns.title: for-in over array (likely bug)
patterns.diagnosis: `for...in` iterates keys (as strings) including inherited ones. For arrays, use `for...of` or `forEach`.
fixes: Use `for (const x of arr)` for values.
Use `arr.forEach((x, i) => ...)` for index+value.

patterns.title: eval blocked by CSP
patterns.diagnosis: Content Security Policy forbade `eval` (or `new Function`).
fixes: Avoid `eval` — there's almost always a better way.
Loosen CSP only if you absolutely must (and understand the risk).

patterns.match: Strict mode code may not include a with statement
patterns.title: `with` not allowed in strict mode
patterns.diagnosis: Strict mode forbids `with`. Use explicit references.
fixes: Bind the object to a name and use `obj.prop`.

patterns.title: Illegal return statement
patterns.diagnosis: `return` outside a function.
fixes: Wrap your code in a function.
If at top level of an ES module, use early-`if` and don't `return`.

patterns.match: Octal literals are not allowed in strict mode
patterns.title: Octal literal in strict mode
patterns.diagnosis: `017` style octal literals don't work in strict mode.
fixes: Use `0o17` instead.

patterns.title: Duplicate parameter name
patterns.diagnosis: Two parameters with the same name in a strict-mode function.
fixes: Rename one of them.

patterns.title: `expect` not defined (test setup)
patterns.diagnosis: Test runner globals weren't injected.
fixes: Make sure the file is matched by your test runner's pattern.
Import `expect` if your config requires it.
Check jest/vitest setup files.

patterns.title: Jest — no active test
patterns.diagnosis: You called an assertion outside `it(...)` / `test(...)`.
fixes: Move the call inside a test block.

patterns.title: EventEmitter — too many listeners
patterns.diagnosis: More than 10 listeners attached to one event (default warning threshold).
fixes: Remove listeners when no longer needed.
If legitimate, `emitter.setMaxListeners(N)`.

patterns.title: Invalid regex
patterns.diagnosis: Your regex literal isn't valid.
fixes: Test on regex101.com (set JavaScript flavor).
Escape special chars inside character classes too.
Check for unbalanced parens or brackets.

patterns.title: `await` outside async function
patterns.diagnosis: You can only `await` inside an `async` function (or at top level of an ES module).
fixes: Add `async` to the enclosing function.
Top-level await needs ESM and a recent Node version.

patterns.match: SyntaxError: Unexpected (?:strict mode reserved word|token) yield
patterns.title: `yield` outside generator
patterns.diagnosis: Only `function*` (generator) functions can `yield`.
fixes: Use `function* name()` syntax.
Arrow functions can't be generators.

patterns.title: extends undefined — bad import
patterns.diagnosis: `class X extends Y` where `Y` is `undefined`. Usually a broken import.
fixes: Check the import — wrong default vs named export.
Print `Y` before the class declaration.

patterns.match: The requested module .* does not provide an export named 'default'
patterns.title: ESM — missing default export
patterns.diagnosis: You imported `default` from a module that doesn't export one.
fixes: Use named imports: `import { thing } from 'mod'`.
Or add a default export to the module.

patterns.match: The requested module .* does not provide an export named '([^']+)'
patterns.title: ESM — missing named export `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: You imported `{1}` but the module doesn't export it.
fixes: Check what the module actually exports.
Spelling, casing, default vs named.

patterns.title: `window` not defined (Node/SSR)
patterns.diagnosis: You used `window` in server-side code.
fixes: Guard with `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')`.
Move browser-only logic into `useEffect` (React) or client components.
Check for SSR frameworks running your code on the server.

patterns.title: `document` not defined (Node/SSR)
patterns.diagnosis: Same idea as `window` — you're running browser code on the server.
fixes: Guard with `typeof document !== 'undefined'`.
Move DOM code into client-only contexts.

patterns.title: `Buffer` not defined (browser)
patterns.diagnosis: `Buffer` is a Node global. Browsers use `Uint8Array` / `TextEncoder`.
fixes: Use `TextEncoder().encode(str)` for bytes.
Polyfill `Buffer` via your bundler if you must.

patterns.title: `setImmediate` not defined (browser)
patterns.diagnosis: `setImmediate` is Node-only.
fixes: Use `setTimeout(fn, 0)` in the browser.
Or `queueMicrotask(fn)`.

patterns.title: Invalid Date
patterns.diagnosis: A `Date` constructor got something it couldn't parse.
fixes: Log the input — it's probably not what you expect.
Parse explicitly with `Date.parse` or a library like `date-fns`.
ISO 8601 strings (`2024-01-15T12:00:00Z`) parse most reliably.

patterns.title: Firefox — too much recursion
patterns.diagnosis: Firefox's version of the stack-overflow message.
fixes: Find the recursive function and add a base case.
Check for circular getters/setters.

patterns.title: npm lockfile issue
patterns.diagnosis: `package-lock.json` is out of sync with `package.json`.
fixes: Run `npm install` (without `ci`).
Delete `package-lock.json` and `node_modules` then reinstall (last resort).

patterns.match: Jest did not exit one second after the test run
patterns.title: Jest didn't exit — open handles
patterns.diagnosis: A timer, server, or DB connection is keeping the event loop alive.
fixes: Close servers/DB clients in `afterAll`.
Clear timers with `clearTimeout`/`clearInterval`.
Run with `--detectOpenHandles` to see what's keeping it open.

patterns.title: Node version mismatch (engine)
patterns.diagnosis: Your Node version doesn't match what a package wants.
fixes: Use `nvm install <version>` and `nvm use <version>`.
Update the package or pin to an older version that supports your Node.

patterns.title: LocalStorage quota exceeded
patterns.diagnosis: You hit the browser's storage limit (~5MB per origin for localStorage).
fixes: Don't store huge blobs in localStorage — use IndexedDB.
Clean up old keys.

patterns.title: command not found — `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: Your shell can't find `{1}` on `PATH`. Either not installed, not on `PATH`, or misspelled.
fixes: Check spelling.
Verify installation: `which {1}` should print a path.
If installed but not found, add its directory to `PATH` in your shell rc.
If using a venv/conda, activate it first.

patterns.title: Permission denied — script/file
patterns.diagnosis: The file isn't executable, or you don't have read access.
fixes: Make executable: `chmod +x ./script.sh`.
Run via interpreter: `bash script.sh` works even without `+x`.
Check ownership: `ls -l script.sh`.

patterns.title: No such file or directory (shell)
patterns.diagnosis: Shell couldn't find the file you referenced.
fixes: Check the path — `ls -l <path>` to confirm.
Tab-complete to catch typos.
Watch for stale `~` expansion or unset variables.

patterns.title: Bash — syntax error
patterns.diagnosis: Something in the script doesn't match the grammar.
fixes: Check for unbalanced quotes or parens.
On Windows-edited files, CRLF line endings can cause weird errors — `dos2unix script.sh`.
Pass through `bash -n script.sh` for a parse-only check.

patterns.title: Bash — unexpected EOF
patterns.diagnosis: The script ended with something still open — a `do`, `then`, `fi`, or quote.
fixes: Every `if` needs a `fi`, every `do` a `done`, every `case` an `esac`.
Check for unterminated heredocs (`<<EOF` without `EOF`).

patterns.title: Bash — bad substitution
patterns.diagnosis: A `${...}` expansion has invalid syntax.
fixes: Watch the operators: `${var:-default}`, `${var%/*}`, `${var//a/b}` — exact placement matters.
Some sh shells don't support all bash expansions — set `#!/usr/bin/env bash`.

patterns.title: Bash history — event not found
patterns.diagnosis: `!` triggered history expansion and found no matching event.
fixes: Quote with single quotes: `echo 'hello!'`.
Or escape: `echo "hello\!"`.
Disable history expansion in scripts: `set +H`.

patterns.title: Bash history — bang quote
patterns.diagnosis: A `!` near a quote triggered history expansion.
fixes: Use single quotes around exclamation marks.
Or `set +H` to disable history expansion.

patterns.title: Argument list too long
patterns.diagnosis: You expanded too many filenames into a single command (`rm *`, `cp ./*`).
fixes: Use `find ... -delete` or `find ... -exec ... +`.
Pipe through `xargs`.
Process in batches.

patterns.title: Killed — OOM or signal
patterns.diagnosis: The kernel killed your process, usually because it ran out of memory.
fixes: Check `dmesg | tail` for an OOM message.
Reduce memory use — stream data instead of loading it all.
If running in a container, raise the memory limit.

patterns.title: Segmentation fault
patterns.diagnosis: A native program tried to access memory it shouldn't have.
fixes: Likely a bug in the binary (or in C code you wrote).
Re-run under a debugger (`gdb`, `lldb`).
If from a package, search for known crashes and update.

patterns.title: Broken pipe
patterns.diagnosis: A pipeline's reader (e.g. `head`) closed before the writer was done. Often harmless.
fixes: If undesired, restructure so the reader consumes everything.
Wrap with `2>/dev/null` if you don't care.

patterns.title: Operation not permitted
patterns.diagnosis: Even root sometimes can't override certain restrictions (immutable files, capabilities).
fixes: Check `lsattr` for the `i` flag (immutable).
On macOS, System Integrity Protection blocks some paths.
In containers, missing capabilities cause this.

patterns.title: Bad interpreter (shebang)
patterns.diagnosis: The interpreter named in the script's `#!` line doesn't exist or has CRLF line endings.
fixes: Make sure the path after `#!` exists.
Use `#!/usr/bin/env python3` for portability.
Run `dos2unix script` to strip Windows line endings.

patterns.title: Script exited due to set -e
patterns.diagnosis: With `set -e`, any non-zero exit kills the script.
fixes: Allow specific failures: `cmd || true`.
Wrap with `if cmd; then ... else ...; fi` if you want to handle failure.

patterns.title: Bash — unbound variable
patterns.diagnosis: With `set -u`, referencing an unset variable is fatal.
fixes: Use a default: `${VAR:-default}`.
Initialize the variable before use.
Check spelling.

patterns.title: Bash — parameter not set
patterns.diagnosis: A required parameter is missing (often inside `${VAR:?msg}`).
fixes: Set the variable before calling.
Pass it via env or argument.

patterns.title: cd: too many arguments
patterns.diagnosis: Usually `cd $path` where `$path` contains spaces and wasn't quoted.
fixes: Quote it: `cd "$path"`.
Always quote variables in shell.

patterns.title: Bash — ambiguous redirect
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote `> $file` where `$file` is empty or has spaces.
fixes: Quote: `> "$file"`.
Set the variable before using it.

patterns.title: kill — no such process
patterns.diagnosis: The PID is already gone (or never existed).
fixes: Confirm with `ps -p <pid>`.
List processes by name: `pgrep -fl pattern`.

patterns.title: xargs — argument line too long
patterns.diagnosis: An item is too big to fit in one exec call.
fixes: Add `-n 1` to xargs to process one at a time.
Use `find ... -exec ... +` instead.

patterns.title: find — paths must precede expression
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote `find -name '*.py' .` — the path has to come before flags.
fixes: Put the path first: `find . -name '*.py'`.
Quote globs to prevent shell expansion.

patterns.title: sed — unterminated substitute
patterns.diagnosis: Your `s/.../.../` command isn't closed properly.
fixes: Check that you have three delimiters: `s/a/b/`.
If the pattern contains `/`, use a different delimiter: `s|/usr|/opt|`.

patterns.title: awk — read error
patterns.diagnosis: awk couldn't read its input.
fixes: Check the input file exists and is readable.
Try the same file with `cat` to verify.

patterns.title: tar — not a tar archive
patterns.diagnosis: The file isn't a tar archive (or it's truncated/corrupt).
fixes: Check with `file archive.tar` to see what it actually is.
Re-download — partial transfers cause this.

patterns.match: gzip: stdin: not in gzip format
patterns.title: gzip — not a gzip file
patterns.diagnosis: Input isn't gzip-compressed.
fixes: Check with `file <name>`.
Don't double-extract — `tar xf` already handles gz.

patterns.title: Missing utility (minimal container)
patterns.diagnosis: Standard Unix tools aren't present in stripped-down images.
fixes: Install: `apt install lsof procps` (Debian) or `apk add lsof procps` (Alpine).
Use BusyBox alternatives where available.

patterns.title: SSH — permission denied (publickey)
patterns.diagnosis: The remote rejected your SSH key.
fixes: Make sure you've added your key: `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.
For GitHub: upload your public key (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`) at github.com/settings/keys.
Test with `ssh -vT git@github.com`.
Generate a new key if you don't have one: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`.

patterns.title: SSH — host key verification failed
patterns.diagnosis: The remote's key doesn't match what's in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.
fixes: If the host legitimately changed, remove the stale line: `ssh-keygen -R hostname`.
Verify the new fingerprint with the server owner before accepting.
Never blindly accept — could be a MITM attack.

patterns.title: SSH — connection refused
patterns.diagnosis: Nothing accepting SSH connections on the remote.
fixes: Is sshd running on the remote?
Right port? Default is 22, but some hosts use a non-standard port.
Firewall blocking?

patterns.title: SSH — remote identity changed!
patterns.diagnosis: The remote's key changed since you last connected. Could be a re-install, or a man-in-the-middle attack.
fixes: If you trust the change (reinstall, key rotation), remove the old line: `ssh-keygen -R hostname`.
Otherwise: don't connect until you've verified with the server owner.

patterns.title: curl (6) — DNS resolution failed
patterns.diagnosis: DNS couldn't resolve the hostname.
fixes: Check spelling of the URL.
Test with `nslookup host` or `dig host`.
Verify network: `ping 8.8.8.8`.

patterns.title: curl (7) — failed to connect
patterns.diagnosis: DNS resolved but the connection was refused or unreachable.
fixes: Is the server actually listening on that port?
Try `nc -zv host port`.
Firewall blocking?

patterns.title: curl (35) — SSL connect error
patterns.diagnosis: TLS handshake failed.
fixes: Server may require a newer TLS version — update curl.
Outdated CA bundle — `brew upgrade curl` or update OS.
Try `--tlsv1.2` or higher explicitly.

patterns.title: curl (60) — SSL certificate problem
patterns.diagnosis: Couldn't validate the certificate.
fixes: Update CA certs (`apt install ca-certificates` or `brew install ca-certificates`).
For dev only: `-k` skips verification (don't ship!).
Trust corporate CA via `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`.

patterns.title: wget — failed
patterns.diagnosis: Similar to curl — DNS, connection, or TLS.
fixes: Test the URL with curl for a clearer error.
Check network and DNS.

patterns.title: npm global install — permission denied
patterns.diagnosis: Don't run `npm install -g` with `sudo`.
fixes: Use a Node version manager: `nvm`, `fnm`, `volta`.
Or set npm's prefix to a folder you own: `npm config set prefix ~/.npm-global`.

patterns.title: Locale not configured
patterns.diagnosis: The locale env var points at a locale not installed.
fixes: Set `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` or `en_US.UTF-8`.
On Debian/Ubuntu: `locale-gen en_US.UTF-8`.

patterns.title: HOME not set
patterns.diagnosis: `$HOME` is empty and `cd` (with no args) has nowhere to go.
fixes: Set `HOME=/path/to/home`.
Common in cron/systemd contexts — export it in the script.

patterns.title: read — arg count
patterns.diagnosis: `read` got the wrong number of variable names.
fixes: Check the `read` invocation syntax.
Use `read -r var` for one value, `read -r a b c` for three.

patterns.title: [ ] — too many arguments
patterns.diagnosis: Usually an unquoted variable that contains spaces split into separate args.
fixes: Quote: `[ "$var" = "value" ]`.
Use `[[ ... ]]` in bash — handles spaces better.

patterns.title: [ ] — unary operator expected
patterns.diagnosis: A variable is empty and `[ -z $var ]` (unquoted) becomes `[ -z ]`.
fixes: Quote: `[ -z "$var" ]`.
Use `[[ ... ]]` for safer behavior.

patterns.title: Arithmetic syntax error
patterns.diagnosis: `$((expr))` had bad syntax — non-numeric value, stray character.
fixes: Make sure all operands are integers.
Quote subshells: `$(( $(date +%s) - start ))` style.

patterns.title: zsh — no glob matches
patterns.diagnosis: zsh aborts when a glob has no matches (bash silently passes it through).
fixes: Quote it: `'pattern'` to pass literal.
`setopt nullglob` to make unmatched globs expand to nothing.
`setopt no_nomatch` to make zsh act like bash.

patterns.title: chmod — file missing
patterns.diagnosis: Target file doesn't exist.
fixes: Check the path with `ls`.
Tab-complete to avoid typos.

patterns.title: PIPESTATUS — pipeline element failed
patterns.diagnosis: A non-last command in a pipeline failed; without `pipefail` you'd never know.
fixes: `set -o pipefail` makes pipelines fail if any element does.
Check `${PIPESTATUS[@]}` after the pipeline.

patterns.title: env — interpreter not found
patterns.diagnosis: `#!/usr/bin/env <thing>` couldn't find `<thing>` on PATH.
fixes: Make sure the interpreter is on PATH.
Check for CRLF line endings in the script.

patterns.title: Bad ${ } substitution
patterns.diagnosis: An invalid expansion form inside `${...}`.
fixes: Some forms are bash-only — use `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, not `sh`.
Check operator placement.

patterns.title: sudo not installed
patterns.diagnosis: Common in minimal containers — `sudo` isn't there.
fixes: Run as root directly (containers often do).
Install sudo if you need it (`apt install sudo`).

patterns.match: make: \*\*\* No rule to make target
patterns.title: make — no rule for target
patterns.diagnosis: You asked make to build something it doesn't know how to make.
fixes: Check the target name spelling.
Run `make help` (if your Makefile supports it) to list targets.
Open the Makefile and find which rules exist.

patterns.title: Not a git repository
patterns.diagnosis: You ran `git` outside a repository (and not in a subfolder of one).
fixes: Run `git init` to start a new repo.
Or `cd` into an existing repo.
Run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to find the nearest repo root.

patterns.match: fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories
patterns.title: Refusing to merge unrelated histories
patterns.diagnosis: Two branches share no common commits. Common after cloning + re-initing, or merging two separate projects.
fixes: Force the merge if you're sure: `git pull --allow-unrelated-histories`.
Often a sign you cloned into the wrong directory or initialized twice.

patterns.title: Git — authentication failed
patterns.diagnosis: The remote rejected your credentials.
fixes: For GitHub HTTPS: use a Personal Access Token, not your password.
Update stored creds: `git credential-manager` or your OS keychain.
Or switch to SSH: change remote with `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:user/repo.git`.

patterns.title: Remote already exists
patterns.diagnosis: A remote named `{1}` is already configured.
fixes: Update it: `git remote set-url {1} <new-url>`.
Or remove and re-add: `git remote remove {1}` then `git remote add {1} <url>`.

patterns.match: fatal: not currently on any branch
patterns.title: Not on a branch (detached HEAD)
patterns.diagnosis: You're in detached HEAD — checked out a commit, not a branch.
fixes: Create a branch from here: `git switch -c new-branch`.
Or jump back: `git switch main`.

patterns.match: (?:fatal|error): pathspec '([^']+)' did not match any file
patterns.title: pathspec didn't match
patterns.diagnosis: Git can't find anything matching `{1}`. Wrong path, deleted file, or a branch name that doesn't exist.
fixes: Check spelling.
If switching branches: list with `git branch -a`.
If checking out a file: confirm with `git ls-files | grep ...`.

patterns.title: Git — bad object
patterns.diagnosis: Git's object database has a damaged or unknown object reference.
fixes: Try `git fsck --full` to find broken objects.
If recoverable: `git fetch` to re-download from remote.
Last resort: re-clone.

patterns.match: fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a merge
patterns.title: Partial commit during merge
patterns.diagnosis: Mid-merge you can't commit just some files — git wants the whole index.
fixes: Stage everything: `git add -A`.
Or finish the merge first, then commit selectively in a new change.

patterns.match: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten
patterns.title: Local changes would be overwritten
patterns.diagnosis: Git won't let you switch/pull because doing so would clobber uncommitted edits.
fixes: Stash: `git stash` then `git stash pop` after.
Commit your work first.
If you want to throw away local changes: `git restore .` (careful!).

patterns.match: error: pathspec '([^']+)' did not match any file\(s\) known to git
patterns.title: pathspec — file not known to git
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` isn't tracked or doesn't exist in the working tree.
fixes: Confirm it's tracked: `git ls-files | grep {1}`.
Check spelling and case (case-sensitive on Linux, varies elsewhere).

patterns.match: error: failed to push some refs
patterns.title: Push rejected
patterns.diagnosis: The remote has commits you don't. Git won't let you overwrite them.
fixes: Pull first: `git pull --rebase` then push.
If your local is intentionally ahead and you want to force: `git push --force-with-lease` (only on your own branches!).
Never force-push to shared branches without coordinating.

patterns.match: error: src refspec ([^\s]+) does not match any
patterns.title: src refspec doesn't match
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to push a branch `{1}` that doesn't exist locally.
fixes: List local branches: `git branch`.
Check spelling.
If you just created it, commit at least once before pushing.

patterns.title: Cannot lock ref
patterns.diagnosis: Git couldn't get a lock on a ref file — usually a stale `.git/refs/...lock` or permission issue.
fixes: Remove stale lock files: `find .git -name '*.lock' -delete`.
Check `.git/` permissions.

patterns.title: Non-fast-forward push rejected
patterns.diagnosis: Your branch diverged from the remote.
fixes: Pull and rebase: `git pull --rebase`.
Then push: `git push`.
Only force-push (`--force-with-lease`) on personal branches.

patterns.match: Updates were rejected because the tip of your current branch is behind
patterns.title: Branch is behind remote
patterns.diagnosis: Remote has commits you haven't pulled.
fixes: Pull: `git pull --rebase`.
Then push.

patterns.title: Merge conflict in `{1}`
